# requireNonDouble

<link-summary>Returns the value after checking that it is not a number with a fractional part.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNonDouble() — Returns the value after checking that it is not a number with a fractional part. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/number</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNonDouble<T>(
  value: T | number,
  message: string = "Expected a value without a fractional part."
): T;
```

A synonym of the `Float` family, offered under the name people reach for first. In JavaScript every number already is a double, so `double` names no runtime distinction of its own.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                                | Type          | Description                                                   |
| :----------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                                  | `T \| number` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a value without a fractional part."` | `string`      | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`T` — the same value, with a number with a fractional part excluded from its type.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                                     |
| :------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is a number with a fractional part. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNonDouble(42); // => 42
requireNonDouble(1.0); // => 1.0
requireNonDouble(1.5); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNonDouble(-0.1); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
